text: I've created `filter.py`. It removed every attack I tried and left a harmless HTML file exactly as it was, byte for byte. I only tested with hand-written inputs in a scratch folder; I didn't run any of the output in a real browser. **How it works:** it scans the file the way a browser's HTML parser reads tags and attributes. It only rewrites a tag when that tag contains something dangerous. Everything else is left as is, including whitespace, line endings (even `\r\n`), entities, comments, tables, headers and safe attributes. It uses only the Python standard library, reads and writes raw bytes so the file's encoding is never changed, and doesn't touch the file at all if there's nothing to remove. **What it removes:** - **Elements, along with their content:** `ipt>` can't reassemble into a working script. - If an attribute value contains `<`, it filters that value too.
